text: The cluster-wide average isn't wrong, it's incomplete. It still answers a real cost-and-capacity question. The fix is additive: keep it, and add the breakdown that would have caught this sooner.
The entire technical lift is a query change — grouping the existing utilization query by the availability-zone node label instead of collapsing it into one number.

The new panel would have shown exactly what Theo found manually: one zone near ninety-six percent, sitting right next to two zones near twenty-four percent, visible at a glance next to the cluster-wide number.
Theo also pushes the alert rule itself to flag zone-level skew, not just the cluster-wide average crossing eighty percent. Next lesson: briefing leadership on the sale and the incident, honestly.
